sentences.text: I remember an important lesson from my childhood.
When I was eight years old, I got a new bike for my birthday.
It was a beautiful, red bike.
It was very shiny and fast.
I was the happiest kid on my street.
I loved my new bike more than all my other toys.
It was my favorite thing.
I rode my bike every day.
I rode it to the park and to my friend's house.
One sunny afternoon, I played outside.
I rode my bike for many hours.
It was a lot of fun.
Later, it was time to go home for dinner.
My mother said, "Please put your bike in the garage.
The weatherman says it will rain tonight."
I heard her, but I wanted to play for five more minutes.
I said, "Okay, Mom.
I will do it later."
But I did not do it.
I forgot about the bike.
I went inside to eat dinner with my family.
Then I watched TV.
I did not think about my bike one time.
That night, it rained very hard.
The wind was strong, and the rain was cold.
I was warm in my bed.
I did not remember my shiny, red bike.
It was outside in the dark and the rain all night.
The next morning, I ran to the yard.
I was excited to ride my bike.
But I saw a very sad thing.
My new bike was not shiny anymore.
It was wet and dirty.
There were small brown spots on the metal parts.
The brown spots were rust.
Rust is very bad for a bike.
My beautiful bike looked old and ugly.
I was very, very sad.
I started to cry.
My mother came outside.
She saw me and the bike.
She did not say, "I told you so."
She just gave me a warm hug.
I knew it was my fault.
I did not listen to her.
I was not a responsible person.
From that day, I learned a big lesson.
You must take care of your special things.
You should listen to your parents because they want to help you.
Now, I am an adult, but I still remember my rusty bike.
It was a sad day, but it taught me a good lesson about responsibility.
I will not make that mistake again.
